model_note: The trial agents were launched on the `opus` alias rather than a pinned model id, because the orchestrating session has no way to pass a pinned id through. The id above is what the session environment reports for the parent; treat it as the nearest attribution available, not a guarantee that every trial resolved to the same weights.

settings.stage1_confirmation: bypassed: no human present; the contract was derived from the brief and recorded in design_spec.md

runs.failure: the final gate passed, but Step 7 export never ran; exports/ is empty

observations: Every run passed its first-page probe with few or no findings, then hit 9-17 blocking findings at the first early gate (pages 5-6). Two error families dominate: sibling root groups whose data-pptx-bounds overlap, and text exceeding its group bounds on one or both axes. The single-page probe cannot see either, because both are cross-module properties.
Every run reached a clean final gate, so the repair loop closes; the cost is 2-4 gate cycles between the early gate and the final one.
text_measure.py call counts differ by an order of magnitude (19 vs 156) with no visible relationship to wall clock or repair rounds. Three samples cannot separate a strategy difference from noise.
Both delivered decks open as editable DrawingML: r1 has 12 slides, 142 native text frames, 78 freeforms and 79 groups, and no pictures. The export is not a screenshot skin.
limits: The trials did not run under the dsh harness, so run_report.py could not read step counts or read lists; checker_calls and text_measure_calls were recovered from each project's validation/workflow.log as the nearest cost proxy.
Stage 1 (communication contract and template choice) was bypassed and AI image generation was disabled. Neither is measured by this baseline.
Visual quality was not reviewed by a human; the verdict covers the checker and delivery only.
two of three runs completed, and the third stopped before export. The pass rate therefore says nothing about a longer session.
